description: GENERATED by scripts/termhost-bench/marker-golden.mjs --write — do not edit by hand. The contract between the JS encoder and Phase 2's raster decoder. `valid` / `invalid` are cell-level vectors: each valid one decodes to its (kind, session, seq) and each invalid one is rejected with exactly its `reason`, checks running in `codec.decode_order`. `rows` are pixel rows ([r, g, b, count] runs): decoding a row by `codec.pixel` must produce exactly its `expected` list, left to right (empty = no candidate in the row). A row whose `note` begins "rule N" pins that step of `codec.pixel.rules`: a decoder departing from the step gets the row wrong.

codec.digit_rule: value[i] = (value[i-1] + 1 + digit[i]) mod 8, value[-1] = 0, digit in 0..6

checksum.rule: h = 0; for d in kind,session,seq digits: h = (h * 31 + d + 1) mod 16787; written as 5 big-endian base-7 digits

codec.overlay: ESC 7, ESC [ row+1 ; col+1 H, then per cell ESC [ 48;5;<index> m SPACE, then ESC [ 0 m, ESC 8

rules: 1. geometry: pixel i spans [i, i + 1); a segment over pixels start..end-1 spans [start, end); for segments A then B, gap(A, B) = B.start - A.end and mid(A, B) = (A.end + B.start) / 2; round(x) rounds half up (every x rounded here is >= 0); arithmetic is IEEE-754 binary64, evaluated as written
2. classify each pixel: a channel <= channel_low_max is 0, >= channel_high_min is 1, anything else is impure; a pixel is pure when all three channels are, value = 4R + 2G + B
3. segments: the maximal runs of pure pixels with one value, numbered left to right; impure pixels lie in the gaps between them

4. first width at segment s, when s is red (4) and s+1 is cyan (3): b1 = mid(s, s+1); if segment s+2 exists, m = mid(s+1, s+2), cyan_wide = gap(s+1, s+2) >= boundary_gap_max * (m - b1) and b2 = cyan_wide ? (s+1).end : m; if it does not, cyan_wide = false and b2 = (s+1).end; w = b2 - b1

5. start: s is a candidate when gap(s, s+1) < boundary_gap_max * w; a candidate with no segment s+2 is wrong_length; otherwise cells = [4, 3], left = b2, next = s + 2, in_gap = cyan_wide, and rules 6-7 repeat while there are fewer than 20 cells (need = 20 - cells)

6. impure gap (in_gap): end = the start of segment next, or the row length when there is none; k = max(1, round((end - left) / w)); append min(k, need) impure cells (null); if all k were appended, w = (end - b1) / (cells - 1); then left = end and in_gap = false

7. segment (not in_gap): if there is no segment next, wrong_length; else g = segment next and h = segment next+1 if any; trailing = (h ? h.start : row length) - g.end; wide = trailing >= boundary_gap_max * w; right = wide ? g.end : (h ? mid(g, h) : row length); span = (right - left) / w; k = round(span); if k >= need, append need cells of g's value, next = next + 1 and stop, leaving whatever lies beyond unchecked (cell 19 may merge into same-coloured content); else if k < 1 or |span - k| > width_tolerance, irregular_cells; else append k cells of g's value (a run k cells wide is k equal cells), w = (right - b1) / (cells - 1), left = right, in_gap = wide, next = next + 1
8. result: the 20 cells (null = impure) go through the cell checks in decode_order, giving {ok: true, kind, session, seq} or {ok: false, reason}; a rejection in rule 5 or 7 is {ok: false, reason}

9. scan: s = 0; while s + 1 < the segment count: if s is not a candidate, s = s + 1; else record its result, then continue at s = next when it decoded ok, or s = s + 1 when it was rejected; the results in order are the row's expected list ([] = no candidate)

rows.name: valid, 6.5 px cells, 2 px blur, quarter-pixel phase
rows.note: rule 4: b1 and b2 are gap MIDDLES, and the gap after cyan is judged against the distance from b1 to its middle, not against cyan's pure pixels

rows.name: pixel-snapped 7/8 px cells, cells 16-18 equal
rows.note: rule 7: w is the running mean (7.47 px by cell 16), so the 23 px run is 3 equal cells: adjacent_cells_equal. Held to the cyan cell's 7 px it would be irregular_cells

rows.name: pixel-snapped 7/8 px cells, cells 2-5 off-palette, cells 6-8 equal
rows.note: rules 5-6: the impure gap opens right after cyan and updates w to 7.4 px, so the 23 px run after it is 3 cells: off_palette. Without that update it would be irregular_cells

rows.name: 6 px cells, a 13 px two-cell run, then a 3 px impure stretch
rows.note: rules 6-7: the stretch is wide against the w before the run (3 >= 0.5 x 6) but rounds to 0 cells against the w after it (6.09 px), so max(1, ...) counts one impure cell: off_palette

rows.name: 10 px cells, exactly 5 px of impure pixels after cell 9
rows.note: rule 7: a gap of exactly boundary_gap_max x w is wide (>=), and round(0.5) = 1 impure cell: off_palette

rows.name: clipped inside the last cell: 4 px of cell 19, 2 impure px, then the row ends
rows.note: rule 7: with no segment after it and a narrow trailing gap, a segment's right boundary is the row end (span 0.6 cell, k = 1); the segment reaching cell 19 needs no width check, so it decodes

rows.name: red-cyan gap exactly half the first width
rows.note: rule 5: w = 12 px between gap middles, and a 6 px red-cyan gap is not < 0.5 x w (strict): no start, no candidate

rows.name: valid with a red-cyan pair inside (cells 15-16, seq 7)
rows.note: rule 9: scanning resumes after the segment that gave cell 19, so the pair inside an accepted marker starts no second candidate

rows.name: 8 px cells, one cell exactly 1.25 cells wide
rows.note: rule 7: |span / w - k| <= width_tolerance is inclusive, so a 10 px cell at w = 8 is one cell and the marker decodes

rows.name: off-palette cell 2, right after the start
rows.note: rules 4-6: the gap after cyan is a whole impure cell (cyan_wide), so decoding starts inside an impure gap: off_palette

rows.name: a 1 px pure sliver of another colour between cells 9 and 10
rows.note: rule 7: the sliver is a segment of its own, 0.2 cell wide; k = 0 fails k >= 1: irregular_cells

rows.name: colour management to the band edges: 0 -> 63 and 255 -> 192 still decodes
rows.note: rule 2: the bands are inclusive, channel_low_max (63) is 0 and channel_high_min (192) is 1

rows.name: one level past the low band: 0 -> 64 is impure
rows.note: rule 2: 64 is impure, so every cell with a 0 channel is impure and no red-cyan start remains: no candidate

rows.name: one level past the high band: 255 -> 191 is impure
rows.note: rule 2: 191 is impure, so every cell with a 255 channel is impure and no red-cyan start remains: no candidate
